headline: 207 caps, 125 goals: Lionel Messi retires from international football
summary: The football legend ends a historic 20-year career with Argentina, leaving behind a legacy of a World Cup title and two Copa América trophies.
details: Lionel Messi has officially retired from international football, ending a historic career with the Argentina national team after more than two decades of service.
The 39-year-old legend made a record 207 appearances for the national team, scoring 125 goals and leading Argentina to victory in the 2022 FIFA World Cup and two Copa América titles.
FIFA President Gianni Infantino praised Messi's 'extraordinary' career, stating that his 'magical talent and humility will be remembered forever.'
Messi's senior debut for Argentina was in 2005, and his final international appearance came in Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
While his time with the national team is officially over, Messi will continue his club career with Inter Miami in the United States.
Football figures and fans worldwide are celebrating the legacy of an 'eternal' Messi, who redefined the beautiful game and inspired millions.
caption:
The end of an era. 207 caps, 125 goals, and a World Cup trophy. Lionel Messi says goodbye to Argentina.

Lionel Messi has officially retired from international football, ending a historic career with the Argentina national team after more than two decades of service.

The 39-year-old legend made a record 207 appearances for the national team, scoring 125 goals and leading Argentina to victory in the 2022 FIFA World Cup and two Copa América titles.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino praised Messi's 'extraordinary' career, stating that his 'magical talent and humility will be remembered forever.'

Messi's senior debut for Argentina was in 2005, and his final international appearance came in Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.

While his time with the national team is officially over, Messi will continue his club career with Inter Miami in the United States.

Football figures and fans worldwide are celebrating the legacy of an 'eternal' Messi, who redefined the beautiful game and inspired millions.

headline_marked: 52 [[Sundarbans bandits from four gangs surrender]] to RAB
headline: 52 Sundarbans bandits from four gangs surrender to RAB
summary: The surrender follows intense surveillance and operations by RAB-6 in the coastal regions to curb kidnapping and extortion.
details: A total of 52 pirates and forest bandits from the Sundarbans and surrounding coastal areas have surrendered to the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB).
The surrender was confirmed by RAB-6 in a press release on Tuesday, September 1.
The bandits belonged to four different gangs: 16 from the Boro Jahangir gang, 15 from the Dulabhai gang, 13 from the Anarul gang, and 8 from the Aftab gang.
According to RAB, these groups had long been involved in criminal activities, including kidnapping and extortion, targeting fishermen, woodcutters, and local residents.
The surrender is attributed to RAB's strict surveillance and coordinated operations, which prompted the gang members to abandon crime and return to a normal life.
RAB-6 stated that necessary legal actions are being taken against the surrendered bandits according to existing laws.
Following the completion of the legal process, they will be handed over to the relevant courts.
caption:

A total of 52 pirates and forest bandits from the Sundarbans and surrounding coastal areas have surrendered to the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB).

The bandits belonged to four different gangs: 16 from the Boro Jahangir gang, 15 from the Dulabhai gang, 13 from the Anarul gang, and 8 from the Aftab gang.

According to RAB, these groups had long been involved in criminal activities, including kidnapping and extortion, targeting fishermen, woodcutters, and local residents.

The surrender is attributed to RAB's strict surveillance and coordinated operations, which prompted the gang members to abandon crime and return to a normal life.

RAB-6 stated that necessary legal actions are being taken against the surrendered bandits according to existing laws.

Following the completion of the legal process, they will be handed over to the relevant courts.
